tier_reason: Peer-reviewed IPDPS 2022 paper (DOI 10.1109/IPDPS53621.2022.00075); two independent WebSearch snippets of its abstract state an average 3.64x speedup over cuSZ's Huffman decoder and 2.43x overall decompression. The artifact repo has the decoders, run.sh scripts and runcusz.sh baseline script with -O3 Makefiles, but no CPU model and no numbers, so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Snippet only (paper abstract via WebSearch; arXiv 2201.09118 and the IEEE/NSF pages are blocked here): average 3.64x speedup over cuSZ's Huffman decoder and 2.43x average improvement of cuSZ's overall decompression, on an Nvidia V100 with eight scientific datasets. The 'above 100 GB/s' throughput figure could not be confirmed from any reachable source and is dropped.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: GCC 8.3.1 and NVCC 11.1 (README); Makefiles in opt-self-sync/ and opt-gap-array/ use CFLAGS -std=c++17 -g -O3 -march=native and NVCC_FLAGS --std=c++14 -O3 with -gencode arch=compute_70,code=sm_70
corrections.caveats: No LICENSE or COPYING file in the repo, so reference only. Numbers come from WebSearch snippets of the paper abstract; the repo README has no numbers and the paper PDF was unreachable (arXiv, IEEE, par.nsf.gov, hgpu.org blocked). Hardware is stated only as 'x86_64 CPU' plus a Tesla V100 32 GB. Baseline is cuSZ's GPU Huffman decoder, not a CPU library. Running the benchmark needs a separate cuSZ build and dataset download (getdata.sh). Last commit 2022-03-01.

notes: Repo exists, 3 stars, 5 commits, last 2022-03-01, no license, not a fork. Metadata in record correct. runcusz.sh times cuSZ's own decompression on HACC, EXAALT, CESM, Nyx and Isabel at error bound 1e-3; benchmark_url set to that script since the record had none.

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed ICPP 2019 paper (DOI 10.1145/3337821.3337888); WebSearch snippet of its abstract confirms up to 17x over 64 CPU threads, 31x over a SIMD decoder and 39x over Zstandard's entropy codec. The repo's demo only compares GPU against its own multicore CPU decoder, has no numbers and no stated hardware, so not A.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: CUDA SDK 9+ (README); Makefile NVCC_FLAGS --std=c++14 -O3 -arch=sm_70 -Xcompiler=-pthread -D CUDA -D MULTI with ARCH = 61 gencode; paper's compiler versions not verified
corrections.caveats: Paper (ACM DL) and its hardware tables were not reachable; speedups are from an abstract snippet and are 'up to' figures, so typical gains are lower and the CPU/GPU models behind them are unknown. The repo demo compares only against its own multicore CPU decoder on synthetic exponentially distributed 256-symbol data, not against Zstandard, so the Zstandard comparison cannot be reproduced from the repo. Decoder supports a single table, radix 2, up to 256 symbols. Makefile sets both ARCH = 61 gencode and -arch=sm_70. Last commit 2019-07-26.

notes: Repo exists, 30 stars, 4 forks, 5 commits, LGPL-3.0 confirmed from LICENSE, last commit 2019-07-26. Record metadata correct; only flags and caveats tightened.

tier_reason: README benchmark table compares Huff0 and FSE against zlibh with the exact numbers in the record, on an i7-5600U with GCC 4.8.4; benchmark code is public (programs/bench.c, programs/zlibh.c, probaGenerator.c) but optimisation flags for the README run are not stated, so first-party C.

corrections.caveats: Benchmark is old (GCC 4.8.4, Broadwell laptop, optimisation flags not stated) and uses only synthetic generated distributions with 32 KB blocks. Baseline zlibh is a weak Huffman. Better modern Huffman decoders exist (see PIVCO-Huffman and hypersonic-rANS entries). zstd itself (facebook/zstd) is on the known list; this entry is the standalone upstream FSE/Huff0 repo, whose dev branch last changed 2024-03-10. The lib/ sources are dual BSD-2-Clause/GPLv2; the test and benchmark tools in programs/ are GPLv2 only.

notes: README numbers match the record exactly; derived ratios (4.5x decode, 2.3x encode) check out. BSD-2-Clause, 1.5k stars, 166 forks, not archived, last commit 2024-03-10 (stale is right).
